topics.label: Atlantic Immigration Program
topics.metaDescription: Atlantic Immigration Program requirements: designated employer, no LMIA needed, and the settlement plan process for New Brunswick, NS, PEI & NL.
topics.lead: The Atlantic Immigration Program is a permanent employer-driven pathway for skilled workers and international graduates settling in New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, or Newfoundland and Labrador. It runs outside Express Entry, with its own dedicated application process, and does not require a Labour Market Impact Assessment.

topics.label: Agri-Food Immigration Pilot
topics.metaDescription: Agri-Food Pilot requirements: eligible occupations, non-seasonal job offer rules, and language/education thresholds for meat processing & farm roles.
topics.lead: The Agri-Food Immigration Pilot is a targeted pathway to permanent residence for experienced, non-seasonal workers in specific agriculture and food-processing occupations — created to address chronic labour shortages in an industry that has historically relied heavily on temporary foreign workers.

topics.label: Rural and Northern Immigration Pilot
topics.seoTitle: Rural and Northern Immigration Pilot (RNIP) Canada 2026 | CMG
topics.metaDescription: RNIP requirements: community-recommended job offers, no LMIA needed, and how the community endorsement process works for participating towns.
topics.lead: The Rural and Northern Immigration Pilot connects skilled foreign workers with job opportunities in smaller Canadian communities that have opted in to attract newcomers — a community-driven route to permanent residence that doesn't require a Labour Market Impact Assessment.

topics.label: Municipal Nominee Program
topics.metaDescription: Canada's Municipal Nominee Program: community-based nomination for smaller and mid-sized towns, modelled on the Rural & Northern pilot.
topics.lead: The Municipal Nominee Program is a newer federal initiative extending the community-driven nomination model beyond the original Rural and Northern pilot communities, letting a broader range of smaller and mid-sized municipalities nominate economic immigrants directly.

topics.label: Business Immigration & Start-Up Visa
topics.seoTitle: Start-Up Visa & Business Immigration Canada 2026 | CMG
topics.metaDescription: Canada Start-Up Visa requirements: designated organization support, language, and funds thresholds. Compare with provincial entrepreneur streams. Free review.
topics.lead: Canada's Start-Up Visa program offers permanent residence to entrepreneurs whose business idea receives support from a designated Canadian organization — a venture capital fund, angel investor group, or business incubator. It sits alongside self-employed and provincial entrepreneur streams as the main routes for business-driven immigration.

topics.label: Temporary Resident to PR Pathway
topics.seoTitle: Temporary Resident to PR Pathway Canada 2026 | CMG
topics.metaDescription: How to transition from a Canadian work or study permit to permanent residence — CEC, provincial streams, and special public policy routes.
topics.lead: This covers the range of routes allowing someone already in Canada on temporary status — a work or study permit holder, most commonly — to transition to permanent residence, typically by qualifying for the Canadian Experience Class, a provincial nominee stream built for temporary residents, or occasionally a targeted public policy pathway IRCC opens for a specific group.

topics.label: In-Canada Refugee Claim
topics.metaDescription: How to file a refugee claim in Canada: eligibility screening, the IRB hearing process, and work permit eligibility while your claim is pending.
topics.lead: A refugee claim can be made by someone already in Canada, or at a Canadian port of entry, who cannot safely return to their home country due to a well-founded fear of persecution or a risk of serious harm.

topics.label: Pre-Removal Risk Assessment (PRRA)
topics.metaDescription: PRRA eligibility and process: who can apply, what new risk evidence is assessed, and what a positive or negative outcome means.
topics.lead: A PRRA assesses whether a person facing removal from Canada would face a risk of persecution, torture, or cruel and unusual treatment if returned to their country of origin. It is generally available only once other avenues — such as a refused refugee claim — have been exhausted.
